correctness.rationale: Identified exact donor supplies and receiver demands from the resolvent; max-flow/min-cut gives necessary and sufficient all-subset inequalities; positivity makes reverse Q well-defined; matrix 1-norm gives uniqueness. Complete-graph cuts reduce to the exact box and a bidirectional star attains each upper face. Exact-rational checks total 1528 case-level tests; finitary experiments are not substituted for proof.

evidence: Berend (2020), §5.3 has examples where sparse topology prevents desired scores but does not give full characterization.
Gölz et al. (2018), §2 uses voters as terminal sinks and gives splittable/confluent load optimization.
Garcia and Romance (2021) is about ordinal rank realization with changing unweighted graph support.
Utke and Schmidt-Kraepelin (2023), §3 has designated casting sinks and a random-walk branching rule.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The inverse target condition can be restated as a transportation feasibility problem with receiver marginals w_i/tau_i-1 and sender marginals (1-tau_j)w_j/tau_j. This restatement may be useful in other Markov formulations, but the inspected primary statements do not present its all-cut equivalence for this voting model.

originality.rationale: Closest full accessible primary texts were compared by equivalent Markov/flow formulations and actual theorem implications. The new claim is an exact fixed-retention inverse target classification and sharp loopless half-vote barrier; prior work supplies forward weights, partial inverse PageRank design, or different casting models. Priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An uncaptured specialist paper may already derive the same fixed-restart trust-graph transportation criterion via inverse PageRank, especially under different names.
No independent external expert or formal proof audit has been conducted.
The no-majority corollary requires all retention fractions equal and forwarding forbids direct self-delegation.

value.rationale: For all finite trust graphs it determines the exact attainable polytope of cast ballot mass, gives a constructive polynomial-time feasibility/witness algorithm, and a sharp universal nonmajority bound on loopless complete networks under uniform retained voting. These address meaningful target control and concentration rather than arbitrary parameter choices or mere recomputation.
